Certified type:
- Category: "Indicator"
- Type designations: ["IND360"]
- Module designation: The characteristics table mentions "Analog load cells", "Digital load cells (POWERCELL)", "Weighing modules (Precision)" — these are configurations the indicator connects to, not the module designation of the indicator itself. Actually for R76, module designation refers to the module per WELMEC. The cert says "Indicator / Terminal". Hmm. The rule says module_designation: "Analog load cell" | "Not applicable" | null. This is an indicator; its module would be... The table describes the indicator with different load cell types. I could set module_designation to null or "Not applicable". Since it's an indicator, probably "Not applicable" is safer? Actually the schema example says "Analog load cell" | "Not applicable" | null. For an indicator, the module designation might be "Automatic weighing process module" — no. I'll use null since not explicitly stated.

Characteristics table: it's a matrix with columns: (blank), Analog load cells, Digital load cells (POWERCELL), Weighing modules (Precision). So this is a config-level matrix — the indicator's characteristics vary by the connected weighing element type (configuration axis). Actually these are more like "module configurations" of the terminal. The axis is like "load cell / module type configuration".

Rows:
- Accuracy class OIML R 76: Analog: (III) or (IIII); Digital (POWERCELL): (III) or (IIII); Precision: (I), (II), (III)
- Weighing range(s): Analog+Digital: Single interval; Precision: Single interval, Multi-interval, Multiple range
- Maximum number of scale intervals (one weighing range): Analog: n ≤ 10000 divisions; Digital+Precision: "-"
- Maximum number of scale intervals (multi-interval or multiple range): Analog: n ≤ 10000 divisions (per (partial) weighing range); others "-"
- Maximum number of weighing ranges: Analog+Digital: 1; Precision: 3
- Load cell excitation voltage: Analog: 5 V DC; others "-"
- Minimum signal input voltage: Analog: Umin = 0 mV; others "-"
- Load cell power supply: Analog "-"; Digital+Precision: 12 V DC
- Minimum input voltage per verification scale interval: Analog: 0,3 µV → 0.3 µV; others "-"
- Minimum load cell resistance: Analog: 43 Ω; others "-"
- Maximum load cell resistance: Analog: 1050 Ω; others "-"
- Fraction of the maximum permissible error: Analog: 0,5 → 0.5; Digital: (merged colspan 2 with Precision): 0
- Load cell connection: Analog: 6-wire (remote sensing); others "-"
- Maximum value of cable length per cross wire section...: Analog: 1571 m/mm²; others "-"
- Temperature range: all: -10 °C / +40 °C
- Power supply voltage: all: 100–240 V AC 50–60 Hz (for Harsh version), 20-28 V DC (not suitable for road vehicle power supply)

The columns are configurations of the indicator (which weighing element type it connects to). So config_level with axis "connected_weighing_element_type" and conditions "Analog load cells", "Digital load cells (POWERCELL)", "Weighing modules (Precision)".

Alternatively, use matrix_tables to preserve the table, and config_level for the characteristics. I'll do both: matrix_tables preserves the raw table; config_level captures key attributes.

Per rules, values should be structured objects with value/unit_symbol. For config_level, values follow same form: {condition, value, unit_symbol}. The schema shows config_level entries: attribute, axis, values[]: {condition, value}. Rule 5 says values follow same structured form: {condition, value, unit_symbol}. I'll include unit_symbol where applicable.

Note footnote markers: none in this cert. Footnotes: none.

Recommendation:
- id: R76, edition: 2006, scheme: A, accuracy_classes: ["I", "II", "III", "IIII"] — the certificate says "for accuracy class (I) or (II) or (III) or (IIII)". Accuracy classes overall: I, II, III, IIII. But per configuration: analog and digital are (III) or (IIII); precision is (I), (II), (III). The recommendation-level accuracy_classes: ["I","II","III","IIII"].

Test reports:
- NMi-2493052-01, 24 December 2020, 55 pages, type_evaluation_report (they are "OIML Type Evaluation Reports")
- NMi-2493052-02, 55? No: 15 pages
- NMi-2493052-03, 21 pages
- NMi-2493052-04, 20 pages
Role: type_evaluation_report for all.

Revision history: none.

Model family: The cert covers one type IND360 with three configurations. Are these models? The table columns are configuration variants. I think it's better to treat as config axis rather than model family. But one could also treat them as three variants. The rule 5 example mentions 2-sensor-row vs 4-sensor-row setups as config axes. The columns here are types of connected weighing elements — configuration. I'll use config_level. Should I include model_family? Rule says include ONLY if cert covers >1 model variant. These are variants of the same model IND360 differing by connected hardware — arguably configs. I'll skip model_family, or include with models? Hmm. The table header "Analog load cells / Digital load cells (POWERCELL) / Weighing modules (Precision)" — these are configurations of the indicator. I'll use config_level only.

Software identification: table with Description/Version/Remarks: Analog 1.xx.yyyy, Powercell 1.xx.yyyy, Precision 1.xx.yyyy. This is a matrix table too. I could add it as another matrix_table, and maybe as characteristics (software_version per configuration). I'll include as matrix_table named "Software identification" and maybe config_level attribute software_version with conditions Analog, Powercell, Precision — but the conditions are different axis than the load-cell config... Actually they match: Analog (analog load cells), Powercell (digital POWERCELL), Precision (weighing modules). Same axis. I could add config_level entry "software_version" with axis "connected_weighing_element_type": Analog → "1.xx.yyyy", Powercell → "1.xx.yyyy", Precision → "1.xx.yyyy". Value is a string pattern. That's fine.

Characteristics extraction for config_level:

Attributes:
1. accuracy_class — values: {condition: "Analog load cells", value: ["III","IIII"]}? Value should be number|string... Rule says value: number | {min,max} | string. "III) or (IIII" — could be string "(III) or (IIII)" or list. Hmm, structured value shape value can be string. I could use value: "III or IIII"? Better keep strings like "(III) or (IIII)". But no trailing punctuation and no footnote markers; parentheses around class are conventional. I'll use "III" and "IIII" — maybe value: ["III", "IIII"]? The strict shape says number | {min,max} | string. An array would violate. I'll use string "III or IIII" for analog and digital; "I, II or III" for precision. Hmm, but rule 1 says canonical labels for attributes, values fine as strings.

Actually maybe cleaner: accuracy_class values: {condition: "Analog load cells", value: "III or IIII"} etc.

2. weighing_range_type — Analog: "Single interval"; Digital: "Single interval"; Precision: "Single interval, Multi-interval or Multiple range" → string.

3. max_scale_intervals_single_range — Analog: value {min: null, max: 10000}? "n ≤ 10000 divisions" → value: {min: null, max: 10000}, unit_symbol: "divisions"? unit isn't standard; unit_symbol "divisions" maybe. Or value: 10000 with note. I'll do value {max: 10000}, unit_symbol "divisions". Only applies to Analog; others "-" (not applicable). For config_level, only record conditions with actual values; skip "-" entries.

4. max_scale_intervals_multi_interval — Analog: ≤ 10000 divisions per (partial) weighing range. Attribute label: max_scale_intervals_multi_interval; value {max: 10000}, unit "divisions"; maybe condition qualifier. I'll keep attribute label with note. Could include "per (partial) weighing range" — can't easily. Fine.

5. max_weighing_ranges — Analog: 1; Digital: 1; Precision: 3. unit null.

6. load_cell_excitation_voltage — Analog: 5 V DC → value 5, unit_symbol "V DC"? Better: value 5, unit "V", and power_supply_type? Rule 3 example splits AC/DC: `power_supply_type: {value: "AC"}`. For "5 V DC" → load_cell_excitation_voltage: value 5, unit "V DC"? The rule splits "V AC" into voltage V + type AC. I'll do load_cell_excitation_voltage: value 5, unit_symbol "V"; and load_cell_excitation_type? Hmm, that's noisy. Simpler: value 5, unit_symbol "V DC"? The rule says pull unit out: unit_symbol "V" and add separate characteristic "power_supply_type" only in the AC example. For DC I'll do load_cell_excitation_voltage: {value: 5, unit_symbol: "V"} and maybe include DC in attribute name? I'll add a config-level attribute load_cell_excitation: "5 V DC"? No — keep structured: value 5, unit "V DC". Hmm.

I think "V DC" as unit_symbol is acceptable-ish but rule 3 prefers splitting. Let me split:
- load_cell_excitation_voltage: {condition Analog, value 5, unit_symbol "V"}
- excitation_supply_type: "DC"? That seems overkill. I'll just do value 5, unit_symbol "V DC"? The strictness... Rule 3: "110-240V AC 50/60Hz → SPLIT into two characteristics". For "5 V DC" I'll do value 5, unit "V" and add attribute load_cell_excitation_supply_type: "DC"? Eh. Actually simpler: unit_symbol "V DC" — many implementations accept. But to follow rules strictly, I'll set unit_symbol "V" and add separate characteristic "load_cell_excitation_supply_type": {value: "DC"} in config for Analog. Hmm, but that doubles rows. Alternatively just "V DC" combined. I'll go with unit_symbol "V" and include the DC in a separate characteristic. Actually, let me reduce noise: I'll use unit_symbol "V DC" for load cell excitation and load cell power supply (12 V DC). The rule explicitly demonstrates AC split but DC in "5 V DC" — I'll split too for consistency: excitation voltage 5 V; type DC.

Hmm, let me not overthink. I'll do:
- load_cell_excitation_voltage: value 5, unit_symbol "V", condition Analog.
- load_cell_power_supply_voltage: value 12, unit_symbol "V", condition Digital/Powercell (merged colspan 2 across Digital and Precision).
- load_cell_power_supply_type: value "DC", condition Digital/Powercell.

7. min_signal_input_voltage — Analog: "Umin = 0 mV" → value 0, unit_symbol "mV". Label: minimum_signal_input_voltage.

8. min_input_voltage_per_verification_scale_interval — Analog: 0,3 µV → 0.3, unit "µV".

9. min_load_cell_resistance — Analog: 43 Ω.

10. max_load_cell_resistance — Analog: 1050 Ω.

11. fraction_of_maximum_permissible_error (plc-like) — Analog: 0.5; Digital+Precision merged: 0. For R76 this is "fraction of the maximum permissible error" p_ind? Value 0.5 and 0. Dimensionless.

12. load_cell_connection — Analog: "6-wire (remote sensing)" string.

13. max_cable_length_per_cross_section — Analog: "1571 m/mm²" → value 1571, unit_symbol "m/mm²". Label: max_cable_length_per_cross_wire_section.

14. temperature_range — all three: -10/+40 °C → value {min: -10, max: 40}, unit "°C". Since same for all conditions, could put in type_level. Yes — temperature range is colspan 3, same for all → type_level: temperature_range {min:-10,max:40} °C.

15. Power supply voltage — all: "100 – 240 V AC 50 - 60 Hz (for Harsh version), 20 - 28 V DC (not suitable for road vehicle power supply)". Split:
- power_supply_voltage_ac: {min:100, max:240} V, note "for Harsh version"
- power_supply_frequency: {min:50, max:60} Hz, "for Harsh version"
- power_supply_voltage_dc: {min:20, max:28} V
- power_supply_type: "AC / DC"
- note: not suitable for road vehicle power supply.

Since colspan 3, these go to type_level. The parenthetical "(for Harsh version)" — is a condition. Hmm, "100-240 V AC 50-60 Hz (for Harsh version), 20-28 V DC". So AC mains applies to Harsh version; DC is the other. I could encode config_level with axis "power_supply_version"? Or keep type_level with attributes:
- power_supply_voltage: {min: 100, max: 240} V AC (harsh version)
- power_supply_frequency: {min:50, max:60} Hz (harsh version)
- power_supply_voltage_dc: {min:20, max:28} V

I could use config_level with axis "version": condition "Harsh version" → voltage 100-240 V AC 50-60 Hz; condition "DC supply" → 20-28 V DC. That's cleaner per rule 5? The temperature range is type-level.

I'll do config_level for power supply:
{attribute: "power_supply_voltage", axis: "power_supply_option", values: [{condition: "AC mains (Harsh version)", value: {min:100,max:240}, unit_symbol:"V"}, {condition: "DC supply", value: {min:20,max:28}, unit_symbol:"V"}]}
{attribute: "power_supply_frequency", axis: "power_supply_option", values: [{condition: "AC mains (Harsh version)", value: {min:50,max:60}, unit_symbol:"Hz"}]}
And note about road vehicle.

Hmm, but maybe simpler as type_level with separate attrs. The instructions allow either. I'll go config_level for power supply to capture the Harsh version condition. Actually, thinking again — rule 3's example splits "110-240V AC 50/60Hz" into power_supply_voltage, power_supply_frequency, power_supply_type. I'll do that at type_level and mention "for Harsh version" via condition... type_level has no condition field. I'll use config_level with axis "power_supply_option". Fine.

Also accuracy classes at recommendation level: I, II, III, IIII.

Now, matrix_tables: preserve the characteristics table. Columns: ["attribute", "analog_load_cells", "digital_load_cells_powercell", "weighing_modules_precision"]. Rows as objects with the attribute names and values (strings as in table, cleaned). This preserves "-" and merged cells info. Also software table.

Also should I populate model_level? These are configs not models. I'll keep config_level only.

Components: The cert is an indicator; the connected load cells/modules are not components of the certified type per se; they're companion devices. I won't add components. Actually "Digital load cells (POWERCELL)" and "Weighing modules (Precision)" are other instruments the indicator works with. The certified type is just IND360. Skip components.

Module_designation: The schema example for load cells: "Analog load cell". For this indicator cert, characteristics table header mentions "Analog load cells" etc. — but module designation field typically for the certified module. I'll set null (omit). Hmm, the certified type is an indicator; module designation "Not applicable"? I'll omit (null) since not stated. Actually rule 8: don't fabricate. Omit.

Description: "Indicator / Terminal" — I can put description: "Indicator / Terminal". The category: "Indicator".
